punchline: A hamburger was supposed to reach 155 degrees; a company told that its burgers were undercooked judged that heat made them too tough.
thirty_sec: In January 1993 Washington state health officials found an unusual number of Seattle-area children with a serious kidney complication. The cause was E. coli O157:H7 in patties from Jack in the Box. More than 700 people fell ill in four states and four children died. The required cooking temperature was 155 degrees, and according to attorney Bill Marler the company had been warned its burgers were undercooked but judged that heat made them too tough.
